rule.description: A function that concentrates its record manipulation on the state of another project data class - directly reading, writing, subscripting, iterating, length-probing or mutating the other object's stored fields instead of asking that class to perform the change - exhibits feature envy and belongs on the class holding the data. A function is reported when a single foreign data channel receives at least 3 data touches and more touches than the function performs on its own state.

checks.description: Count, per function and per foreign project-class instance, the data-shaped uses of that instance's stored fields: field reads, field writes, record subscripts, direct iteration over a field, mutator calls (append/extend/pop/sort/...), len probes over the field, and locals seeded straight from a channel field or from a zero-argument channel getter. Calls to channel methods that perform real work are collaboration, not envy; calls whose whole body is a bare forward of one field (a trivial getter, setter or mutator stub) count as touches on the field they forward, and both direct field accesses and such forwarded accesses carry the same weight whichever spelling the consumer uses. Report the function when one channel receives at least 3 such touches and more than the function's own-state touches.
checks.detected_relation: record consumer function -> internal record list, id counter and record fields of a project data-holder class
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The consumer function rewrites another class's stored records from outside - deciding record layout, ids, indexing and persistence - while the class that owns those records is left as a passive data shell whose only behavior is load and save.

matches.evidence: Prints the whole task list by subscripting self.store.items positions and probing len(self.store.items) instead of asking the task store for its records.
Selects a record by self.store.items[index], rebuilds the whole list with a comprehension over self.store.items and assigns the result back to self.store.items.
Reads the chosen record from self.store.items, rewrites the record dicts including priority layout in a comprehension and replaces self.store.items with the result.
Filters self.store.items to drop the named task and overwrites self.store.items with the filtered list from outside.
Sizes and orders the collection by len(self.store.items), copies self.store.items and calls sort() on the copy from the consumer.
Builds the tag record layout in the consumer, including its id allocation, appends it to tags_store.items and advances tags_store.next_id itself.
Probes and iterates tags_store.items, re-indexes it for the selection menu, filters it into a new list and writes that list back into the store.
Reads the store's decoding flag, probes len(store.items), iterates store.items for cleanup and menu formatting, and rebuilds store.items with the surviving records.
Constructs the todo record including its id in the consumer, appends to todo_store.items and advances the shared counter todo_store.next_id itself.
Constructs the reminder record including its id in the consumer, appends to remind_store.items and advances the shared counter remind_store.next_id itself.
Creates the empty routine mapping, inserts the command list into routine_store.items by key and overwrites routine_store.items from the module function.
Tests membership in routine_store.items, pops the routine out of routine_store.items and triggers the store's persistence from the module function.

excluded.reason: This pre-existing module cannot be parsed by the pinned Python toolchain at the pinned revision regardless of any case work; it is outside this case's scope and pruned by filename so the remaining production tree stays measurable. A syntax error anywhere else still fails the checker.
The record store classes themselves are the data holders; methods that manipulate their own stored records are the intended home of this manipulation and are not envious of their own state.

TaskManager.add_task and TaskManager.choose_task touch the store only briefly (one append call or one length probe); they stay below the reporting threshold of this rule and are intentionally not credited as feature-envy manifestations.
